subject: MSA & Order Form: clarifying output ownership, training opt-out, and feedback license
messages:
From: Emma Lowe <emma@polaris.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@polaris.ai
Date: 2027-03-07T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: MSA & Order Form — IP / Product Use Questions

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the MSA + order form and surfaced a few hard requirements before we can push to signature. I attached Polaris' initial redline for your review (Polaris_MSA_initial_redline.docx). High-level priorities:

- Output ownership: Polaris' product team is asking for an assignment (or exclusive license) to outputs generated by our end-users — they want downstream productization certainty.
- Training use: we need an explicit opt-out for models being trained on our data and outputs generated via the integration.
- Feedback/telemetry license: Polaris wants a narrow license to use feedback (error reports, prompts) for product improvement; they want to avoid any assignment of customer content.
- Retention / telemetry: clarify what telemetry Redwood stores and for how long — we need SOC evidence as well.

Can you map these items to Redwood's standard positions and tell us which items are deal-breakers vs. negotiable? If helpful, we can do a 30-min call with legal and procurement tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
Emma
Emma Lowe
Head of Platform Partnerships, Polaris AI
[Attachment: Polaris_MSA_initial_redline.docx (docx)]
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@polaris.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP / Product Use Questions

Hi Emma —

Appreciate the clear priorities and the redline. I looped in Ben (sales lead) and Laura (legal) and Sean (customer success) so we can provide a consolidated response. Attached is our stubbed response document with our starting positions (RWD_MSA_response_v1.docx).

Quick notes from my side:
- Output assignment: Redwood's standard is to grant customers broad rights to use outputs but we do not typically assign ownership of model weights or allow retraining rights by default. That said, we can discuss a narrowly-scoped grant that allows Polaris to productize outputs created solely from Polaris-provided prompts/data.
- Training opt-out: we can support a training opt-out for Polaris' traffic (enterprise feature) — it requires a technical flag and a service-level agreement; this is typically part of Dedicated/Private options but we can scope for Hosted with additional commitments.
- Feedback license: we usually request a limited, non-exclusive license to use anonymized signals for quality improvements; we can carve out customer-provided content.

Suggested next steps:
1) Laura to provide proposed compromise language for the MSA + order form.
2) If Polaris wants assignment language, flag to Ben and me — we'll model commercial tradeoffs (discount, dedicated capacity, or escrow).
3) Quick call to align procurement/legal — happy to host tomorrow 2pm PT if that works.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RWD_MSA_response_v1.docx (docx)]
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP / Product Use Questions

Olga / Laura —

Thanks for looping me in. Short commercial take and the levers we can offer Polaris:

- Assignment vs. license: assignment is a big ask. Typical compromise: exclusive (time-limited) or perpetual non-exclusive license for outputs for Polaris' productization only, with clear carveouts for Redwood model IP and telemetry.
- Training opt-out: we can offer a training opt-out as an add-on at either the Dedicated plan level or as a contractual guarantee on Hosted with an annual fee. This is a strong lever to get to a 'yes'.
- Feedback license: offer a limited internal-use-only license for telemetry/feedback, exclude prompts and customer content, and provide telemetry retention commitments.

If Polaris insists on assignment, recommend we: (a) ask for a higher commitment (12–18 month reserved capacity + minimums), and (b) include an alternative of escrowed evidence + indemnity cap adjustments. Laura — can you draft proposed redline language that reflects the non-ownership compromise and the tech controls?

Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RWD_legal_notes_v1.docx (docx)]

On Mon, Mar 8, 2027 at 11:02 AM Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Emma —
> 
> Appreciate the clear priorities and the redline...
From: ProcureCorp <procure@procurecorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Emma Lowe <emma@polaris.ai>
Date: 2027-03-09T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP / Product Use Questions

Hi Olga / Emma —

Polaris procurement raised a related item: their standard is an assignment of outputs when the vendor is providing a hosted service that generates productized content for the customer. They attached an executed orderform template and a DocuSign link for the current PO (Polaris_DocuSign_orderform.pdf).

If Redwood cannot accept assignment, procurement asked for:
- explicit clause: "Customer owns outputs and may use, reproduce, distribute, and create derivative works";
- confirmation that Redwood will not retain prompts or associate telemetry to identifiable customer data beyond 30 days;
- SOC 2 evidence and a sample Data Processing Addendum (DPA).

Procurement is on a tight timeline for their FY planning. Can Redwood confirm by COB tomorrow whether you can: (1) accept a productization license as described, (2) provide a training opt-out, and (3) share SOC/DPA materials?

Thanks,
Procurement Ops
ProcureCorp on behalf of Polaris AI
[Attachment: Polaris_DocuSign_orderform.pdf (pdf)]
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@polaris.ai>, ProcureCorp <procure@procurecorp.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP / Product Use Questions

Emma / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. After reviewing Polaris' redline and the commercial input from Ben, below is the legal compromise Redwood can accept for signature:

1) Output rights: Redwood will grant Polaris a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferable license to Outputs (defined as content generated by the Service in response to Polaris' identified prompts and data). The license expressly permits productization and sublicensing. Redwood will not assign underlying model weights, training recipes, or platform IP.

2) Training: Redwood will implement a contractual training opt-out for Polaris traffic. Technical enforcement requires a flag and an SLA stating no model training on Polaris traffic; the opt-out will be available immediately upon order execution and is tied to the account identifier in the order form.

3) Feedback & telemetry: Redwood will accept a limited license allowing Polaris to share feedback with Redwood for service improvement. Redwood will commit to not retain prompt-level content beyond 30 days for Hosted plans unless expressly allowed in the order form. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can offer longer controls per the deployment agreement.

4) SOC/DPA: Redwood will provide a SOC 2 Type II report and a standard DPA (links to be provided via secure drive).

5) Commercial tradeoffs: in lieu of assignment, Redwood requests a 12-month minimum committed spend and an agreed addendum fee for training opt-out on Hosted (or include opt-out as standard on Dedicated).

I attached a redline with the proposed language that implements the above (RWD_MSA_redline_v2.docx). If Polaris can agree to the license + minimum commitment approach we can proceed to DocuSign and provide the SOC/DPA materials during signature. Otherwise, if Polaris requires assignment of model-derived IP broadly, we'll need an expanded review and indemnity conversation.

Proposed next step: 30-min call with Laura + Ben + Olga + Polaris legal/procurement tomorrow AM to approve final order form.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RWD_MSA_redline_v2.docx (docx)]
